_comment: Risk-path rule table for claude-workflow itself. This repo ships no product
and moves no money, so there are no financial rules — but the tools in cmd/
DECIDE what gets reviewed everywhere else, and config/ plus .claude/ hold the
rule tables that are the gate. A wrong change here disables review silently
across every project that uses it, which is why cmd/ and the configs are the
highest tier in this repo rather than the lowest.
Semantics are the same everywhere: risk is the MAX over matched rules,
components the UNION, financial an OR, and a file is presentational only if
every rule it matched is. Adding a rule can only ever raise risk.
scaffold is false: these paths have been reviewed by a human.

rules.note: The binaries that decide risk tiers, run the gates and drive the iteration loop. A defect here is not a local bug — it changes what gets reviewed in every consuming project.
The gate itself. config/gates.json decides which checks run; a project's risk-paths.json decides what counts as money. Editing these is editing the safety net.
Role and skill definitions are executed by agents against production code. Wrong instructions produce wrong work at scale, but unlike cmd/ a human reads them at each use.
A change here can DISABLE a check rather than fail one, so it is never presentation.
Fixtures encode the assertions the tools are verified against. Weakening one weakens the verification, so this is not presentation.

gate_signals.note: Environment-driven behaviour switch in tooling that gates other repos.
Anything that can turn a check off. In this repo specifically, a skip or waiver path is the highest-value thing to review.
Defaults that let a missing answer read as a passing one.
